basis: Skin hypopigmentation, neurologic impairment and progressive sensorineural deafness define the syndrome. Hearing loss occurs in 30-79%; megacolon is only 5-29%.

decisions.otologic: primary: progressive sensorineural deafness is a defining component of the syndrome, supported by HPO frequency of 30-79%.

basis: Developmental impairment and epilepsy define disease. Left ventricular hypertrophy occurs in 1/1 HPO-assessed patient; cardiac frequency remains uncertain because of the tiny sample.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: structural cardiac involvement is documented in 1/1 assessed patient; follow the supplied HPO frequency, with substantial sampling uncertainty.

basis: Ciliary airway disease with chronic sinusitis in 3/3 and recurrent middle-ear inflammation in 2/2. Situs inversus and dextrocardia alone do not establish organ damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: dextrocardia (1/2) and situs inversus describe position; no damaging cardiac malformation or dysfunction is documented.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: chronic sinusitis in 3/3 supports intrinsic airway disease associated with this ciliary disorder; sinuses belong to the pulmonary axis.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; progressive deafness affects most patients (>50%). Muscle wasting is secondary to denervation; sluggish pupillary responses do not establish eye damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal weakness and atrophy reflect peripheral nerve degeneration; direct skeletal-muscle disease is not established.

basis: Benign sympathetic neuronal tumor. HPO intestinal polyposis/neurofibromatosis (30-79%) represents syndromic associations, not usual direct gut involvement; adrenal dysfunction is unproven.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: intestinal neurofibromatosis and polyposis are associated syndromic conditions; their HPO frequencies do not establish direct gut damage across ganglioneuromas.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease; neurologic dysfunction, hepatopathy and damaging retinal/optic disease each commonly exceed 30%. Common hearing loss is omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinal degeneration and optic disease commonly exceed 30% across Zellweger spectrum; potentially severe visual loss merits retention under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: sensorineural hearing loss commonly exceeds 30% and qualifies clinically, but is omitted under the cap after neurologic, hepatic and ocular damage.

basis: Persistent neutrophil deficiency impairs innate immunity; recurrent infections and lymphopenia occur in 30-79%. Nonimmune describes etiology, not preserved immune defense.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: chronic neutrophil deficiency constitutes impaired innate immunity, supported by recurrent infections in 30-79%; an autoimmune cause is not required.

basis: Central and peripheral neurodegeneration defines SCA3. Ophthalmoplegia (34/57) reflects neural ocular-motor dysfunction; muscle atrophy reflects denervation.

decisions.ocular: none: common ophthalmoplegia and nystagmus arise from neurologic degeneration; direct disease of the eye or optic nerve is not established.

basis: Rapid MPS VI has defining skeletal dysplasia; damaging corneal clouding and cardiac valvular disease each affect most (>80%). Common airway and ear disease omitted under the cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: severe dysostosis multiplex and progressive joint restriction are defining features of rapidly progressing MPS VI, affecting nearly all patients.

basis: Cyanide directly blocks oxidative phosphorylation, producing characteristic severe lactic acidosis and acute neurologic and cardiovascular dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: direct inhibition of cellular respiration produces characteristic severe lactic acidosis, a defining acid-base disturbance of cyanide toxicity.
